html:
William of Orange, called William the Silent, led the revolt of the Low Countries against Spain and is known as the father of the Dutch nation.

A great noble who had served Charles V, he opposed the persecution of Protestants under Philip II. From 1568 he led the Eighty Years' War, raising armies and money, and the rebel provinces made him their leader. The relief of Leiden in 1574, by breaking the dykes to flood the land, was one of his successes.

Philip put a price on his head, and in 1584 a Catholic Frenchman shot him in his home at Delft, one of the first heads of state killed with a handgun. His sons led the war after him. The Dutch national anthem, the Wilhelmus, is about him, and the royal House of Orange descends from his family. See the Netherlands and Leiden University.
sum: William of Orange, called William the Silent, led the revolt of the Low Countries against Spain and is known as the father of the Dutch nation.
